scope: Roll back rejected simulation updates and contain their error at the production200ms loop; preserve valid private commits and retry semantics. No real database access or deployment.
rootCause: Full tick checkpoints were atomic in SQLite, but GameWorld had already changed live HP/resources/drops/NPC/defense state and did not undo it on failure. The production timer also allowed the exception to escape.
changes: Per-tick TickUndo records first entity preimages and affected dictionary/Map entries only. Reverse rollback deletes newly introduced fields, preserves root entity references and restores prior NPC clock and life generations.

New monster/drop entries, expired drops/active entries, survival, NPC simulation/damage, defense ammunition/timestamp and spikes HP participate. Successful NPC-movement-only/private-player/full-checkpoint behavior remains on existing paths.
The production loop catches a tick error and returns before its visibility/state broadcast, allowing later ticks to retry. No new database writer, table, protocol, attack cost or timing grace.

verification.independentReview: Design and final implementation reviewed independently; no P1/P2 found. Review-requested previous accepted NPC-frame and latest private-shot cases included.
redGreen: Rejected defense-death checkpoint originally left turret3→2, target respawned with an inventory drop and removed the expired drop. Fixed version restores exact pre-tick gameplay state/life context and retries one real death.

Rejected NPC checkpoint originally retained target damage, advanced windup/cooldown and a newly discovered monster. Fixed version removes the new entity, restores optional fields/NPC clock, then retries the same frame once.
Removing only the production tick catch causes actual socket recovery test to fail because the server stops. Exact source restored and recovery passes.
regressions: Already committed private ammunition/replay ledger survives failed shared death and is consolidated on successful retry.
One accepted unsaved NPC movement frame is retained when the following frame fails; only the rejected frame's new targetId and state changes are removed.
Failed starvation death restores survival interval, inventory, drop absence and life generation; retry creates only one real drop.
Existing pure-survival rollback, shared defense recovery, body expiry, map/weapon context, visibility and fire replay/rate tests remain passing.

copyScope.explanation: The one serialization is the attempted original durable checkpoint, not an undo copy. Untouched floor reference remains identical. Existing pure-survival600-floor test still sees zero world serializations.
copyScope.limit: This verifies work scope, not throughput or native frame/latency performance.

actualProductionFaultRecovery.method: Unique OS-temp SQLite, actual production server/timers/WebSocket with controlled authoritative clock. A trigger rejects only shared-world UPDATE after startup and negotiation; private player rows remain writable. No runtime grants/reset used.
actualProductionFaultRecovery.healthAndSocket: HTTP health and WebSocket ping remain live
actualProductionFaultRecovery.checkpointWhileRejected: Expired drop still present and private shot row/handled persist

testHarnessCorrections: Initial new assertion forgot camp creation/entry were already in handled; corrected to compare the captured full pre-tick ledger rather than erasing valid history.
First guard mutation did not match CRLF and stopped without modification; normalized matching subsequently produced the expected server-stopped failure, then restored the source.

remaining: Previous dense eight-connection native gate still has one over-fast refusal; no new performance acceptance score is claimed.
This recovery claim covers simulation ticks. Connect/disconnect and other lifecycle save-failure policies are a separate remaining audit.
Real siege capacity, all growth/economy calibration and long-term scale remain broader-goal work. Goal active.
